email.body1:
Blaine, saw Teamworks close its $235M Series F and add Opteamal and Sportlogiq to the AI sports stack.

Growth that fast usually puts more in-market programs in play than business development can cover before the new motions ramp. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Teamworks off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Blaine, quick follow-up for Teamworks.

Post-raise, board expectations on pipeline usually jump faster than headcount, and most teams don't actually know how many meetings they need to hit the new number. The gap shows up late and the quarter turns into a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Teamworks needs this quarter, plus where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Blaine, last bit of proof for Teamworks.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Teamworks' reply rate likely compares to other fast-scaling software companies. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Blaine, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. The fundraise-to-integration stretch keeps a business development team busy for a while.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your BD motion? I'll tailor it to Teamworks either way.
